text:
Posted by Jim Brewer on Mar 23rd, 2018 // No Comments 
Waverton Investment Management Ltd trimmed its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 1.4% during the fourth quarter, HoldingsChannel reports. The firm owned 735,925 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 10,167 shares during the period. Apple comprises 7.3% of Waverton Investment Management Ltd’s holdings, making the stock its biggest holding. Waverton Investment Management Ltd’s holdings in Apple were worth $124,541,000 at the end of the most recent quarter. 
A number of other hedge funds and other institutional investors also recently added to or reduced their stakes in the business. Pure Financial Advisors Inc. lifted its holdings in Apple by 18.1% during the 4th quarter. Pure Financial Advisors Inc. now owns 20,421 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $3,456,000 after buying an additional 3,130 shares in the last quarter. Union Bankshares Corp raised its position in shares of Apple by 8.5% during the 4th quarter. Union Bankshares Corp now owns 53,784 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $9,101,000 after acquiring an additional 4,201 shares during the last quarter. Sit Investment Associates Inc. raised its position in shares of Apple by 1.1% during the 4th quarter. Sit Investment Associates Inc. now owns 440,730 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $74,585,000 after acquiring an additional 4,990 shares during the last quarter. White Lighthouse Investment Management Inc. bought a new stake in shares of Apple during the 4th quarter valued at $5,187,000. Finally, Chesley Taft & Associates LLC raised its position in shares of Apple by 43.3% during the 4th quarter. Chesley Taft & Associates LLC now owns 120,675 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $20,422,000 after acquiring an additional 36,449 shares during the last quarter. 61.33% of the stock is currently owned by institutional investors. AAPL has been the subject of several recent research reports. Vetr cut shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating and set a $178.70 target price for the company. in a research report on Thursday, November 23rd. Nomura set a $185.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Monday, November 27th. UBS set a $190.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Monday, November 27th. Tigress Financial restated a “strong-buy” rating on shares of Apple in a research report on Wednesday, December 6th. Finally, KeyCorp restated a “buy” rating and issued a $192.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Thursday, December 7th. One investment analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-two have issued a buy rating and two have given a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. The stock currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $201.69. Shares of Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) opened at $168.85 on Friday. Apple has a 52-week low of $138.62 and a 52-week high of $183.50. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a current ratio of 1.24 and a quick ratio of 1.20. The firm has a market cap of $869,026.25, a P/E ratio of 17.35, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.29 and a beta of 1.19. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share for the quarter, beating analysts’ consensus estimates of $3.82 by $0.07. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. During the same quarter last year, the business posted $3.36 earnings per share. The company’s quarterly revenue was up 12.7% on a year-over-year basis. equities research analysts expect that Apple will post 11.43 EPS for the current fiscal year. 
In other Apple news, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, January 5th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total value of $2,733,733.98. Following the sale, the insider now owns 13,739 shares in the company, valued at $2,401,302.42. The sale was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is accessible through this link . Company insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock.
